Indirect Restorations

Why Choose Inlay & Onlay Over Direct Fillings

Inlays and onlays are precision-crafted in a lab, offering superior fit, strength, and aesthetics compared to direct composite fillings — ideal for moderate to large cavities.

Precise Laboratory Fit

Unlike chair-side fillings, inlays and onlays are fabricated in a dental lab using digital impressions for a precision fit that eliminates gaps and minimizes future decay risk.

Superior Strength

Porcelain and zirconia inlays/onlays are stronger than composite fillings, resisting fracture and wear. They can withstand heavy chewing forces for 10–15+ years with proper care.

Natural Aesthetics

Porcelain and zirconia perfectly mimic tooth enamel — matching color, translucency, and sheen. They don’t stain or discolor over time like composite fillings.

Tooth Structure Preservation

Inlays and onlays require less tooth removal than crowns. They restore damaged areas while preserving healthy enamel — a more conservative long-term approach.

Longer Lifespan

Clinical studies show inlays and onlays last 10–15+ years on average — significantly longer than composite fillings, which typically need replacement every 5–7 years.

Better Value Long-Term

Though initially costlier than fillings, inlays and onlays eliminate the need for repeated replacements — making them more economical over a 15-year period.

Restoration Types

Inlay vs. Onlay Explained

The key difference: inlays fit within the tooth’s cusps, while onlays extend over one or more cusps to protect weakened tooth structure.

IN

Inlay

Fits inside the tooth between the cusps — used when cusps are structurally sound and don’t require coverage

ON

Onlay

Extends over one or more cusps to protect weakened tooth structure — provides additional strength and prevents fracture

📐

CAD/CAM Precision

Both are designed digitally and milled from a solid block for perfect marginal fit and long-term seal

💎

Material Options

Porcelain for natural aesthetics on front teeth, zirconia for maximum strength on back molars

Treatment Journey

Your Inlay/Onlay Procedure

Standard two-visit protocol — first visit for preparation and impression, second visit one week later for permanent bonding.

1
Visit 1 — Day 1

Tooth Preparation & Digital Impression

Decay is removed and the cavity is prepared with precise margins. A digital 3D scan captures the exact shape and size of the prepared cavity. A temporary filling protects the tooth for one week.

  • Local anesthesia for comfort
  • Decay removal & cavity prep
  • Digital intraoral scan taken
  • Temporary filling placed
  • Lab fabrication begins (5–7 days)
2
Lab Phase — Days 2–7

CAD/CAM Fabrication

Your inlay or onlay is digitally designed and milled from a solid block of porcelain or zirconia in VeaHealth’s partner lab. Color is precisely matched to your natural tooth shade.

  • Digital design in CAD software
  • CAM milling from solid block
  • Shade matching & glazing
  • Quality control inspection
  • Sterilization & packaging
3
Visit 2 — Day 7–10

Permanent Bonding

The temporary filling is removed. Your custom inlay/onlay is tried in to verify fit and bite. Once confirmed, it’s permanently bonded using dental adhesive. Final polishing ensures a smooth, natural feel.

  • Temporary filling removed
  • Inlay/onlay fit verification
  • Bite adjustment if needed
  • Permanent adhesive bonding
  • Final polishing & care instructions

Patient Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between an inlay and an onlay?

An inlay fits within the tooth’s cusps (the raised points) and is used when the cusps are still structurally sound. An onlay extends over one or more cusps to provide additional protection and strength when the cusps are weakened. Your dentist will determine which is appropriate based on the extent of damage.

How long do inlays and onlays last?

With proper care, porcelain and zirconia inlays/onlays last 10–15+ years on average — significantly longer than composite fillings (5–7 years). Longevity depends on oral hygiene, bite forces, and avoiding habits like grinding or chewing ice.

Is the procedure painful?

No. Both visits are performed under local anesthesia. You’ll feel pressure during preparation but no pain. Some sensitivity is normal for a few days after bonding as the tooth adjusts to the new restoration.

Porcelain or zirconia — which is better?

Porcelain offers superior aesthetics and is ideal for visible teeth (premolars, upper molars). Zirconia is stronger and better for back molars that endure heavy chewing forces. VeaHealth’s dentists will recommend the optimal material based on the tooth location and your bite.

Can I eat normally after the procedure?

Yes. After the temporary filling (first visit), stick to soft foods on the opposite side. Once the permanent inlay/onlay is bonded (second visit), you can resume normal eating within 24 hours. Avoid extremely hard foods like ice or hard candy to prevent chipping.

How many days in Istanbul are required?

Standard protocol requires 7–10 days total. First appointment for preparation and scan, then a 5–7 day wait while the lab fabricates your restoration, then the second appointment for permanent bonding. VeaHealth can arrange hotel accommodations and sightseeing tours during the wait.

Is the warranty valid internationally?

Yes. VeaHealth’s 5-year warranty on inlays and onlays is valid worldwide. If a restoration fails due to defect or bonding failure, VeaHealth coordinates repair or replacement — either remotely via a partner clinic in your country or with a return visit to Istanbul.

Why is it so much cheaper in Istanbul?

Lower operating costs (lab fees, rent, staff salaries) in Turkey allow VeaHealth to offer the same premium materials and techniques at 60–70% less than UK/US prices. The quality is identical — same porcelain and zirconia brands, same CAD/CAM technology, same clinical standards.
